note: UMCS reports more than one million scientific entomological specimens in several preservation forms, including 11,000 microscopic preparations. The collection began with the university's establishment in 1944 and grew through research and international exchange; the preparation count is not merged with dry or wet specimens.

note: The University of Silesia Hemiptera collection contains more than 9,000 aphids as microscopic preparations and more than 9,000 scale insects in the same form, alongside pinned specimens and amber inclusions. The digitization project scans microscopic preparations while checking each label's taxonomic, locality, date and collector information, making the slide-label unit central to collection control rather than treating digitization as a substitute for the objects.

note: The National Museum Diptera subcollection separately reports more than 250,000 dry specimens, extensive alcohol material and 30,000 microscopic preparations. title: Algagyűjtemény: Pantocsek József kovamoszat-preparátumai
citation: Magyar Természettudományi Múzeum, “Algagyűjtemény,” current collection record (2026), Pantocsek József diatom preparations.
tags: Hungary; Budapest; diatoms; Pantocsek József; 918 preparations; war loss; surviving collection
note: The museum identifies József Pantocsek's 918 diatom preparations as the most valuable microscopic component of its algae collection. Those surviving preparations represent only about one fifth of Pantocsek's original collection, the remainder having been destroyed during the Second World War. The record therefore documents both a bounded slide corpus and catastrophic collection loss.

title: Medveállatka Gyűjtemény

note: This collection is catalogued explicitly by microscope slide (`tárgylemez`): 211 slides, including 11 Bakony holotypes and one paratype, from material collected and identified by Gyula Alfonz Iharos between 1943 and 1967. The unit of record is the slide itself, making this an unusually clean collection-register case.
